synopsis: The three chains are expert assessments: an open-source core with in-house integration, a model-based engineering stack with heavy-machine physics, and an integrated commercial chain with a partner; “lowest”, “middle” and “highest” indicate relative cost and integration posture, not dollar budgets, because almost every commercial vendor is quote-only [f16155, f16156, f16157]. The lowest-cost chain supports camera/lidar testing, deformable-terrain machine dynamics and scripted scenarios, but validated radar, physics-based ultrasonic, correlated weather effects and qualification evidence require major work; scarce skills and manufacturer-owned integration mean low license cost need not mean low total cost [f16160, f16161, f9281, f9284]. The middle-cost chain couples machine physics to controls through FMI and supports MIL, SIL and HIL, but lacks broad validated multi-sensor weather physics and large-scale coverage-driven scenario management, with module prices unpublished [f13239, f13328, f16164, f16165]. The highest-cost chain offers physics-based simulation of all four sensor types, large-scale regression and partner capacity for a four-month window, yet cannot guarantee off-road realism or eliminate manufacturer correlation tests, and no public evidence establishes end-to-end off-road automatic-braking validation [f16169, f16170, f16171]. At every cost level, the recommended “fourth architecture” allocates tests across fast functional testing, medium-fidelity dynamics, selective high-fidelity simulation, HIL and targeted physical correlation, with allocation determined by sensitivity and correlation work rather than assumption [f16172, f16173].
